Overcoming all odds, the Jacksonville Jaguars have won the Superbowl 28-27 over the Seattle Seahawks!

The improbable season ended in spectacular fashion as Linebacker Myles Jack forced and recovered a fumble by Russel Wilson and walked into the end zone untouched with under a minute remaining. The Jaguars managed to maintain focus on the ensuing drive and stymied the Seahawks in their last-ditch efforts to take back the lead.

Team owner Shahid Khan was proudly hoisted the Lombardi Trophy saying, "this is evidence that the little guy CAN overcome outrageous odds and defeat the undefeatable." This marks the first time in history that a team with a losing regular season record has won the Superbowl and sparks an interesting question as to who will be favorites next year.

The Jaguars first big break came in the preseason when the division rival Colts' Andrew Luck's knee was completely blown out in practice in a freak accident when an undrafted free agent, Khahid Shan, fell into the quarterback coming off a block. Questions were raised about the mysterious player who had hoped to be the first Pakistani national to play in the NFL. After the incident he quietly quit the team and moved back to Pakistan and has refused interview requests out of embarrassment.

The Texans and Titans put together futile efforts as usual during the regular season giving the Jaguars their third division crown.

The next stroke of luck for the team came when their wild card round match-up was announced to be the Bengals who continued their history of solid regular season play and miserable post-season collapses.

Their second round matchup proved to be just as favorable as the Broncos who, despite finding some success in the regular season this year, played their 5th quarterback in 3 years and the inexperience of the rookie showed, getting picked off 5 times, thrice by Jalen Ramsey.

It seemed even more sure that the Jaguars were the team of destiny when Tom Brady accidentally fell down a flight of stairs in the Patriots' team hotel the night before the AFC Conference Championship and broke his hip. As a result, the Patriots couldn't come together to fill the void left on the team and the Jaguars advanced.
